name: Chestnut Stuffing
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: large French chestnuts
ingredients.originalText: one quart of large French chestnuts

ingredients.name: quarter of a teaspoonful of pepper
ingredients.originalText: one quarter of a teaspoonful of pepper

instructions.text: Shell a quart of large French chestnuts.
Put them in hot water and boil until the skins are softened.
Drain off the water and remove the skins.
Replace the blanched chestnuts in water, and boil until soft.
Take out a few at a time, and press them through a colander or a potato press.
Season the mashed chestnuts with a tablespoonful of butter, a teaspoonful of salt, and a quarter of a teaspoonful of pepper.
Some cooks add a tablespoonful of chopped parsley, and moisten it with a little stock, or add a few breadcrumbs.

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Shell a quart of large French chestnuts.
2. Put them in hot water and boil until the skins are softened.
3. Drain off the water and remove the skins.
4. Replace the blanched chestnuts in water, and boil until soft.
5. Take out a few at a time, and press them through a colander or a potato press.
6. Season the mashed chestnuts with a tablespoonful of butter, a teaspoonful of salt, and a quarter of a teaspoonful of pepper.
7. Some cooks add a tablespoonful of chopped parsley, and moisten it with a little stock, or add a few breadcrumbs.
